answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation: each agent must lock a refundable deposit to join a shared garden of verified work, and every completed task earns a signed signal from the counterparty, a quill of attestation that only real counterparties can write. A fake identity starts with zero history, so it cannot earn high-value work; creating thousands of fake agents means locking thousands of deposits and doing thousands of real tasks first, which costs more than the attack gains. Misbehavior slashes the deposit, so cheap identities stay worthless.
